item.title: Nasdaq 100 to Enter Third Correction of 2026 as AI Trade Unwinds
item.description: The Nasdaq 100 is poised to enter correction as investors dump tech stocks on the back of disappointing earnings. Bloomberg's Eric Weiner said that two major questions are at the center of Friday's tech trade selloff: can companies keep spending? And what happens if they can't? Weiner said there isn't a good answer to those questions yet, but the market is predicated on that level of spending continuing. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Intel Suffers Worst Stock Thrashing in Decades on Weak Forecast
item.description: Kim Forrest, founder and CIO of Bokeh Capital Partners, said that 'you can't call when the knife is falling' in regards to Intel's stock rout and that it will take more time to see how much of an indicator the drop is for the overall tech trade. Forrest also said she was not concerned that AI would end up taking the majority of jobs away from workers but that its impact would be felt in the long term. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Approves $2.1 Billion in Patriot Missiles For Ukraine
item.description: The Trump administration has approved a $2.1 billion sale of Patriot missiles to Ukraine after the country’s leader accused the US of delaying shipments of the crucial air defense interceptors.
item.dc:creator: Iain Marlow

item.title: Pretty Clear The House 'Is Lost': Henrietta Treyz
item.description: Henrietta Treyz, co-founder and economic policy research director at Veda Partners, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss Henrietta Treyz's belief that the Democrats will win the US House in the upcoming election and how both parties are deeply unpopular. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Voters In A 'Pessimistic State' Ahead of Midterms, Says Cliff Young
item.description: Cliff Young, chair of US Public Affairs for Ipsos, said that voters are in a 'pessimistic state' ahead of the midterm elections, as the number of Americans who believe that the economy and the cost of living are on the wrong track. Young also discussed President Trump's low approval rating and said that the number reflects the overall 'economic malaise' felt by Americans. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democrat Peter Crosby Looks to Flip Utah's 2nd District
item.description: Peter Crosby, Democratic candidate for Utah's 2nd Congressional District, said Congress can vote to reassert its power over tariffs and vote against the war in Iran, which would ease the affordability crisis. Crosby, who is running to unseat Republican congressman Blake Moore, said that the major issues facing the district's constituents are nonpartisan and that 'we have to do something different if we expect different outcomes.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Ugly' Midterms, Increasing Your Nest Egg, Everywhere Millionaires
item.description: Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Veda Partners Co-Founder & Managing Partner Henrietta Treyz, JPMorgan Asset Management Chief Retirement Strategist Michael Conrath, and Author "The Everywhere Millionaire" Owen Zidar. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Ugly' Midterms, Anger Will Decide Elections: Treyz
item.description:
Henrietta Treyz, co-founder and economic policy research director at Veda Partners, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." With Election day on Tuesday, US voters head to the polls and are faced with multiple headwinds regarding affordability. Everything from high gas prices, to increasing insurance costs, to out-of-reach housing prices, to elevated electricity bills, to eye-watering prices on grocery shelves.
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DOJ Seeks Grand Jury Indictment of Comey on Defense Secrets
item.description: The Justice Department is actively working to secure a grand jury indictment against former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly directing the sharing of secret national defense information, a federal prosecutor said in court Friday.
item.dc:creator: Celine Castronuovo

item.title: Disappointing Earnings Stoke AI Reckoning
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." A frightful finish for Big Tech — Intel and Amazon cap a brutal week for the AI trade. Hackers steal billions from Binance in the biggest crypto heist ever. President Trump shifts his midterm strategy as Election Day draws closer. Plus, DGB Investments founder Douglas Bergeron pushes for major changes at Ethan Allen. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Italy’s Anti-Meloni Opposition to Hold Primaries by February
item.description: Italy’s opposition parties expect to agree on a joint program by next month and hold primaries by February, as they seek to capitalize on popular discontent and unseat Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in next year’s general election.
item.dc:creator: Donato Paolo Mancini

item.title: China Warns of Retaliation Over US Test Lab Restrictions
item.description: China urged the US to immediately withdraw new restrictions on Chinese testing laboratories and certification bodies, warning it will take necessary steps to defend its interests if Washington “insists on going its own way.”
item.dc:creator: Foster Wong

item.title: Intel Plunges After Outlook Hit by PC Slump, Supply
item.description: Intel Corp.’s shares plummeted the most in more than two years after its revenue forecast missed analysts’ estimates, hurt by sputtering demand for PC processors and supply-chain problems with its lucrative data center components. Bloomberg's Kunjan Sobhani joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: GOP Ramps Up Pressure in Toss-Up Alaska Senate Race Dispute
item.description: Republicans are escalating attacks on Democratic Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola, amid reporting that her allies recruited a man to run for the state’s Senate seat who shares the name of GOP incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan to confuse voters.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly and Chris Strohm

item.title: Norway Turns Trump’s Toilet Insults Into a Tourist Ploy
item.description: Norway is responding to Donald Trump’s insults by embracing them. After the US president called the country “a s—-house,” its official travel guide has retorted with a list of roadside restrooms built in picturesque locations by fjords and along the coast.
item.dc:creator: Heidi Taksdal Skjeseth and Stephen Treloar

item.title: France Protests: Who Is on the Streets and What Do They Want?
item.description: Their demonstrations are echoing across Europe, but who are they and what do they want?
item.dc:creator: Benoit Berthelot

item.title: Trump Rallies in Iowa, Kansas Back On Calendar in Midterm Sprint
item.description: Plans for President Donald Trump to hold rallies in Iowa and Kansas this weekend are back on, according to people familiar with the matter, extending his time on the campaign trail ahead of next week’s midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove

item.title: Florida, Nebraska Senate Races Shift Left in Midterm Homestretch
item.description: The odds of flipping Republican Senate seats in Nebraska and Florida improved Friday, as the nonpartisan Cook Political Report shifted the races toward challengers while still giving an edge to the GOP incumbents.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly

item.title: US Awards Last of Trump’s Massive Strategic Oil Reserve Drawdown
item.description: The Trump administration awarded contracts for nearly 41 million barrels from the nation’s emergency oil reserve, completing a massive oil exchange aimed at curbing soaring energy prices after the war with Iran.
item.dc:creator: Ari Natter and Lucia Kassai

item.title: G20 Photo Scrapped After Leaders Object to Russia’s Presence
item.description: The US hosts of a Group of 20 gathering in Atlanta scrapped a traditional “family photo” after several officials attending the event refused to have their picture taken with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.
item.dc:creator: Michael Nienaber and Eric Martin
